answer: The prevalence of the gardening pathway for introducing non-native plants is not uniform across habitat types but is context-dependent — highest in semi-natural, lower-urbanization, stream-adjacent habitats and lowest in the most urbanized and agricultural habitats. In the Catalonia/Barcelona data (632 plots, 481 recorded non-native species introductions), the gardening share of introductions per habitat is highest in Wetlands (55.8%, 95% CI 42.3–68.4) and Coastal (53.5%, CI 38.9–67.5), intermediate in Riparian (36.5%) and Urban (29.8%), and lowest in Croplands (18.5%, CI 12.3–26.9); this habitat-by-pathway structure is statistically significant (chi-square test of independence, chi2=75.2, df=18, p=5.8e-9; robust subset with n.total>=20: chi2=53.7, df=8, p=8e-9). The pattern is associated with landscape context rather than being a simple urbanization effect: the highest gardening prevalence occurs in habitats with low urban land cover and close proximity to streams (Wetlands, Coastal), whereas the Urban habitat (mean urban.2009.500m ≈ 0.57) and Croplands (mean cropland.2009.500m ≈ 0.45) show lower gardening shares, and a plot-level model links higher urban land cover to a lower gardening share (p≈0.01; cropland and road distance non-significant). This is consistent with gardening being the dominant modern pathway overall (gardening rises from 16.8% of pre-1500 introductions to 75.2% in 1985–2019) and with gardening-introduced invasive species having narrower invaded niches (niche breadth 0.46 vs 0.72) and occupying fewer habitat types (1.95 vs 2.49) than species from other pathways.

payload.hypothesis: The gardening pathway's prevalence is context-dependent across habitat types: highest in semi-natural, low-urbanization, stream-adjacent habitats (Wetlands ~56%, Coastal ~54%) and lowest in the most agricultural and urbanized habitats (Croplands ~19%, Urban ~30%), a statistically significant habitat-by-pathway pattern (chi2=75.2, df=18, p=5.8e-9) that is associated with lower urban land cover (p~0.01) rather than with a simple urbanization effect.
payload.workflow: Parsed the four files with their true delimiters (invaded_niche and temporal are TAB; invasion_success is comma; phylogenetic tree is Newick). Verified internal consistency (n.gard+n.unint+n.agfo==n.total in all 632 rows). Aggregated pathway counts per habitat, computed gardening share = sum(n.gard)/sum(n.total) with Wilson 95% CIs, flagged low-confidence habitats (n.total<20), ran chi-square independence on habitat x pathway (all and robust subset), built a descriptive landscape-context table plus Pearson correlations and an exploratory plot-level binomial GLM (gardening vs non-gardening on n.total>0 plots), cross-checked with temporal trends and invasion_success. Executed script: final_analysis.py.
